chunks: And he, peace be upon him, said:

Indeed, the close angels descend on every Friday with silver sheets and golden pens. They sit at every door of the mosques upon chairs of light, and they write down those who attended the Jumu‘ah prayer: the first, the second, and the third, until the Imam comes out. Then when the Imam comes out, they fold up their scrolls.

key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: the leader whose emergence marks the closing of the record
key_terms.الْجُمُعَةَ: the Jumu‘ah prayer attendance being recorded
key_terms.الْمَسَاجِدِ: the mosques at whose doors the angels sit
key_terms.الْمَلَائِكَةَ: the angels who descend and record attendance
key_terms.الْمُقَرَّبِينَ: those brought near to Allah, indicating exalted angels
key_terms.جُمُعَةٍ: Friday, the day of congregational worship
key_terms.صُحُفَهُمْ: their scrolls or sheets upon which attendance is written

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the virtue of arriving early for Jumu‘ah prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the virtue of arriving early for Jumu‘ah prayer and portrays the attendance as being recorded by the close angels. It emphasizes the sanctity of Jumu‘ah and the importance of prompt presence before the Imam emerges.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: "Indeed, the close angels descend every Jumu’ah, carrying silver tablets and golden pens. They sit at the doors of the mosques on chairs made of light and write down the names of those who attend the Jumu’ah prayer—the first, the second, and the third—until the Imam comes out. When the Imam comes out, they roll up their scrolls."
